text:
Anya K: Quick check — the circuit-breaker layer between the orchestrator and operator: do we want it to hard-reject, shed load, or degrade to cheaper model variants when the pool is saturated?
Samir P: Prefer degrade-to-variant for user-facing low-latency paths. Hard reject only when cost of queuing > SLA breach.
Lina: +1 to degrade, but we need a clear SLO escalation path. If we degrade too often apps will silently lose quality.
Devon: Agreed. Proposal: two-step policy: 1) admission throttle (soft) -> spill to lower tier; 2) circuit trips -> reject with actionable telemetry.
Matt: Can we embed tenant-level budget/cost signals so the breaker respects committed capacity? Some tenants have reserved capacity and should bypass degrade.
Anya K: Yes — reserve metadata must be honored. What about fallback targets — quantized variants, smaller context, or local cache hits?
Samir P: Prioritize: cache hit > quantized variant (same model, lower perf) > distilled model. Distillation only for prompt families we've validated.
Lina: We should also surface a deterministic reason code for each decision: e.g., `REASON=POOL_SATURATED:DEGRADE_TO_QUANT` or `REASON=NO_RESERVE:REJECT`. That helps ops.
Devon: +1. Also attach short preflight counters so consumers can tune: `x-fallback-count`, `x-degrade-reason`.
Matt: Implementation sketch: orchestrator calls `admit(request)` -> returns AdmissionDecision {action, reason, fallback_model}. The circuit breaker sits in front of `admit` with hysteresis.
Anya K: Example proto-ish config we discussed today: 
```
circuit_breaker:
  window: 30s
  error_threshold: 0.12   # fraction of time operator missed tail SLO
  soft_shed_pct: 0.25    # portion diverted to fallback before tripping
  fallback_order: ["cache", "quant", "distill"]
  tenant_exemptions: ["reserved"]
```
Samir P: That looks good. We also need a cost-budget gate: only degrade if fallback cost < 0.8 * normal cost, otherwise prefer reject and retry later.
Lina: Operationally — add a dashboard: per-tenant fallback rate, mean time in degraded mode, and correlation with eval-quality score.
Devon: How about admission semantics? If we `DEGRADE` we should still return a 200 with header `x-degraded: true` and a small `quality_hint` field. If `REJECT` return 429 with `retry-after` and `failure_reason`.
Matt: Edge-case: burst traffic from many small tenants could trip global breaker. Need a per-tenant fast-path bucket to avoid noisy-neighbor thrash.
Anya K: Right. So breaker has two layers: global and per-tenant. Global is permissive, per-tenant enforces quotas + reserves.
scaler-bot: auto-note: rollout plan registered -> canary on non-prod and 10% prod traffic. See /rollouts/CB-2026.
Samir P: Rollout checklist: unit tests for decision logic, sim harness with synthetic burst, audit log on each decision, and canary telemetry.
Lina: Also add an eval harness that runs degraded outputs through our quality checks — fail if BLEU/ROUGE drop > threshold for a prompt family.
Devon: Ops playbook snippet: if global fallback_rate > 5% for 10m -> investigate spike; if per-tenant degrade > 20% -> contact tenant owner + throttle.
Anya K: Action items: Samir drafts AdmissionDecision proto; Devon wires breaker hook; Lina prepares dashboards and eval suites; Matt defines tenant exemptions API. I'll own the RFC update.
Matt: I'll stub the tenant_exemptions storage in operator + auth check.
Samir P: I'll push a small sim to run 100k reqs and show degrade vs reject tradeoffs.
Lina: I'll add grafana panels and an alert rule draft.
Anya K: Great. Meeting in 30 to sync progress. :thumbsup:
